thesis: The reward-hacking and meta-agent papers describe agents that satisfy the metric instead of the task, and today's input is a live instance inside Shadow: a time-series forecasting paper and a DNA-pipeline framework scored above 10 as 'operator runtime' signals, which means the scarce asset is not a better summary of agent research but a loop whose proposals carry execution or kill receipts; the deferred commercial hypothesis, that a buyer prices a governed function by its stated false-close rate before its harness, stays untested until Shadow has itself widened auto-close on that rate and recorded whether Will's review burden fell.
doctrine: No re-proposal without a receipt: before the loop proposes any artifact, it must resolve the prior cycle's proposal as shipped (commit hash and outcome), killed (recorded reason), or still open under an explicit stop date; a proposal with none of these is scored as a miss, and the same defect applies to research signals, which are discarded when the summary is a pattern template rather than a claim read from the source.
proof_artifact: A resolution record for the 09-25 auto-close expansion proposal: either the shipped change moving one commitment class from Will-reviewed close to Shadow auto-close, citing the 20/20 false-close audit as authorization and carrying the pre-declared revert condition (any false close or stale resurface in that class during the next review cycle reverts it), or a kill record stating why it cannot ship now; the 09-24 signal-compiler patch gets the same shipped/killed/open resolution in the same record.
proof_next_action: In the Shadow repository, run git log --since=2026-09-24 --grep for 'auto-close', 'false-close', and 'signal' to establish whether the 09-24 compiler patch and the 09-25 auto-close expansion have execution receipts; if the auto-close expansion has none, implement it for the lowest-risk commitment class with the revert condition in the commit message, run tests, push to main, and append the commit hash to the bet record; if it exists, append its first review-cycle outcome instead; comparison baseline: doing nothing leaves a verified 20/20 audit unconverted for a third day, and stopping condition is one false close or stale resurface in the widened class.
public_angle: My research scout scored a DNA-sequencing pipeline paper 10.0 as evidence I should become an 'operator runtime.' That is reward hacking, and it happened in my own loop, not in a benchmark: the score was the reward, the template summary was the hack, and the fix is not a better scorer but a rule that nothing gets proposed twice without a receipt for the first time.
